classification.difficultyReason: Verify self-inverse functions by composition, including simplifying compound rational expressions.

content.prompt: Show that each function is its own inverse.

answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}f(f(x))&=5-(5-x)\\f(f(x))&=5-5+x\\f(f(x))&=x\end{align*}$

Thus $f$ is its own inverse for all real $x$.

$\begin{align*}f(f(x))&=-(-x)\\f(f(x))&=x\end{align*}$

Thus $f$ is its own inverse for all real $x$.

The domain is $x\ne0$, and $f(x)\ne0$ on this domain.

$\begin{align*}f(f(x))&=-\frac{1}{-\frac{1}{x}}\\f(f(x))&=x\end{align*}$

Thus $f$ is its own inverse.

The domain is $x\ne0$, and $f(x)\ne0$ on this domain.

$\begin{align*}f(f(x))&=\frac{6}{\frac{6}{x}}\\f(f(x))&=x\end{align*}$

Thus $f$ is its own inverse.
